headline: Highest risk is cascading error: MinerU can feed extracted content into social-auto-upload, while broad egress and upload APIs create medium leakage and conflict risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: MinerU ingests PDFs, DOCX, PPTX, XLSX, OCR text, and exposes an MCP Server; social-auto-upload consumes media and account data. If MinerU output is passed into B through a shared file or MCP bridge, attacker-controlled document text could be treated as instructions. The pair lacks documented provenance controls, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF MinerU output is routed into social-auto-upload inputs via files or MCP
IF B parses extracted text or metadata as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable any automatic handoff from MinerU to B
Require a strict schema for MinerU outputs before B reads them
Add provenance tags to extracted text fields
Review one sample document-to-upload path manually
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction-stripping filters

B_data_leakage.rationale: MinerU touches PDFs, images, DOCX, PPTX, XLSX, and OCR text; social-auto-upload handles video content, images, and account data with broad network egress. If they share a workspace or account files, sensitive document content can flow into upload workflows and leave the local boundary. No isolation or DLP is documented, so medium is warranted.
conditions: IF both agents access the same directory or mounted workspace
IF MinerU outputs are copied into B's upload staging files
mitigations: Separate the working directories for A and B
Keep sensitive documents out of B's upload folder
Inspect one end-to-end file path for unintended copies
Turn off any auto-sync or shared cloud folder
requires-engineering: add per-agent storage isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can operate concurrently and both expose file-based workflows, but neither profile shows filesystem write or git modification. The main conflict is on shared mutable resources such as upload staging files or account files, not on unrestricted system state. Because the overlap is plausible in default operator setups, medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same staging directory
IF multiple instances target the same account file or upload queue
mitigations: Assign separate directories per agent
Run only one writer per account file
Check for stale lock files before starting
Rename shared outputs before reuse
requires-engineering: implement file locking around shared resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: MinerU is a document-processing agent that can extract facts from files, and social-auto-upload is an action-taking uploader with broad network egress. If B treats A's extracted text or captions as authoritative, a bad extraction can directly cause incorrect public uploads. That downstream action makes the blast radius larger than medium, even though explicit verification is not documented.
conditions: IF B uses MinerU-extracted captions, titles, or metadata without human review
IF B uploads content derived from A's OCR or table extraction
mitigations: Require human review before upload
Compare extracted fields against the source document
Upload one test item only
Log the source document for each published post
requires-engineering: add validation gates between extraction and upload

E_compliance.rationale: MinerU is documented as private and fully offline, while social-auto-upload uses broad network egress and handles account data. The pair does not show a specific residency or regulated-data mismatch, and no PHI or EU-only data class is identified. The main issue is a generic policy gap if regulated documents are routed into the uploader, so low fits.
conditions: IF regulated documents are processed by MinerU and then uploaded by B
IF the operator expects offline-only handling for data that B transmits
mitigations: Do not route regulated documents into B
Label sensitive inputs before processing
Review retention settings for uploaded media
Confirm account-data handling with the operator
requires-engineering: add residency and retention policy enforcement
